title: O, Cease, My Wandering Soul
description: O, Cease, My Wandering Soul in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 474 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Ark of Safety”, where the book credits them to the Episcopal Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, cease, my wan-dering soul, On rest-less wing to roam; All this wide world, to ei-ther pole, Has not for thee a home.

lines: All this wide world, to either pole,
Has not for thee a home.
O, haste to gain that dear abode,
And rove, my soul, no more.
There, sweet shall be thy rest,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
